extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organizations, fact-checking practitioners, media researchers, and the general public interested in collaborative election fact-checking
extracted.subtask_description: Organizing and running a collaborative, event-focused fact-checking initiative (a pop-up newsroom) to detect and counter disinformation during an election, including workflows, tools, partnerships, audience engagement, and content dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pop-up newsroom approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a temporary newsroom around a specific event (e.g., an election or natural disaster) to coordinate fact-checking and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approach can be used for global or local initiatives; organizers should hold launch workshops and design workflows specific to community partners and the event. For Verificado 2018, organizers from Pop-Up Newsroom, AJ+ Español, and Animal Político worked with organizations across Mexican states and held a launch workshop attended by journalists from across the country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital newsroom coordination and core team
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate work through a digital newsroom with a core group of journalists (e.g., a ~30-person core coordinating team).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a central digital coordination structure for day-to-day collaboration; larger groups can be formed for specific tasks (e.g., debate fact-checking). Verificado used a core group of about 30 people and expanded into larger teams as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen participation via messaging hotlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable citizen participation by providing channels (e.g., a WhatsApp hotline) where users can submit messages for verification and debunking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hotlines help detect trending topics quickly and incorporate audience labor into workflows; Verificado's WhatsApp hotline had over 10,000 subscribers and received tens of thousands of messages, enabling rapid identification of claims to verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content selection criteria: checkability and public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Select content for verification based on the likelihood it can be checked and its level of public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize items that can be meaningfully verified and that matter to the public; this guides effective use of limited verification resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collaborative verification tools and tailored workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Use collaborative verification tools (e.g., Check by Meedan) and match verification paths/workflows to the types of content involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat different content types (videos, WhatsApp chains, tweets) with different verification steps. Check served as a central project database for curating, annotating, and verifying content and for tracking assignments and preventing duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment tracking and duplication prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Track assignment of staff to steps and use systems to prevent duplication of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central database or tool should record who is working on each claim and which verification steps are completed; Verificado used Check to manage assignments and avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior editor adjudication and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior editors assign a final status to each claim (e.g., True/Verdadero, False/Falso, Misleading/Engañoso).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final editorial decisions should be centralized to maintain consistency in labels and public messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create strong, shareable visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally create strong visuals that are easy to read, searchable, and shareable to communicate verification results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design verification content to be visually appealing and native to social media formats so it is more likely to be shared; Verificado produced visuals and videos tailored for social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-media-first dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Make fact-checking and verification content native to social media: shareable, fresh, visually appealing, and presented in platform-appropriate ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hashtags, memes, emojis, and platform-native formats to increase reach and engagement; Verificado emphasized social-media-first strategies and used #QuieroQueVerifiquen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and engagement style: civil, friendly, humorous
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a civil, friendly tone and use humor (memes, emojis) where appropriate to engage audiences while maintaining factual rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing scientific, fact-based reporting with approachable humor can help relate to readers and encourage participation; Verificado intervened in conversations with a friendly tone to keep discussions civil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about structure, funding, and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about organizational structure, funding sources, and reporting methodology to establish legitimacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish decision trees for investigating claims and make notes from the verification process publicly available to increase trust and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish verification process materials (decision tree, notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly outline and publish the processes for validating claims (e.g., a decision tree) and make verification notes public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public documentation of verification processes and notes helps audiences and partners understand and trust the work; Verificado posted such materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding control to identify authorized sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and control branding and how it can be used, so people can identify authorized sources and know who to trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear branding prevents counterfeit information from being mistaken for official verification output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner network roles and amplification strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with a network of partners (local and national media, universities, civil society) with defined roles: local partners do local verification; large broadcasters amplify to wide audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage partners’ strengths for local knowledge, subject expertise, and distribution; Verificado had ~90 partners and varied roles among them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage academics and subject-matter experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve academics and subject-matter experts to bring expertise and help respond quickly to technical or specialized claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts can improve accuracy and credibility across a wide range of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debate-specific team structure and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Form topic-specific teams for live events (e.g., debates) that transcribe statements, identify claims, verify them, and publish timely responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For debates Verificado formed teams (~20 per group or topic-based teams) that tracked politicians, transcribed statements, selected claims (e.g., ~40 claims), and produced verifications distributed during and after debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt monitoring to event phases (election day focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust monitoring priorities as events evolve (e.g., pre-election vs. election day) to focus on relevant disinformation topics like voting processes and ballot instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As disinformation topics shift (e.g., misleading voting instructions), workflows and alerts should be adapted to detect and address those narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience education on verification techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce educational content teaching readers how to verify online content (reverse image search, bot detection, distinguishing official info).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helping audiences learn verification techniques builds resilience; Verificado's tutorials included a video on reverse image search that received over 1 million views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure impact with engagement and output metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track metrics such as hotline messages/interactions, number of notes/visuals/videos produced, pageviews, and partner amplification to assess reach and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verificado tracked inputs (e.g., 18,000 messages in first week), outputs (over 400 notes, 100 visuals, 50 videos), and web traffic (millions of visits) to quantify impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure partnerships with tech platforms and funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek support and collaboration from technology platforms and journalism funders (e.g., Facebook Journalism Project, Google News Initiative) to access resources and distribution channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform partnerships can provide funding, distribution, and technical cooperation (e.g., WhatsApp collaboration) that improve detection and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific monitoring and social tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ monitoring and social media tools (e.g., CrowdTangle, Tweetdeck, Check by Meedan, Krzana) to find, curate, and analyze content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select tools that fit the workflow and content types being monitored; Verificado used a suite of tools for discovery, tracking, and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational staffing ratios and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain effective staffing and coordination ratios (e.g., reported ~1 coordinator to 5 fact-checkers) to manage workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate coordinator-to-fact-checker ratios can help supervise verification work, assign tasks, and ensure quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'declaracionitis'—corroborate statements beyond publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish statements by public figures without analysis; always corroborate information rather than relying on mere publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing unexamined statements neglects basic journalistic corroboration and can propagate misinformation; Verificado called out this practice as problematic.
